translations.text: He leads from the south, to the assembly of the Lord, a bright gathering of chancels [?]: Columba with hundreds of churches, a broad candle.
Fair his struggle; kingship with God after his course, noble kingship since he reached the end of life's path.
He broke desires; he gave a covenant [?] ... of the glen [?]; Columba laid upon them fair bonds [?].
Candle of Connacht, candle of Scotland, wonderful lord; with scores of curraghs he crossed [?] ... thirty ... [?].
He crossed the wave-filled, mighty, great [?], maned, seal-filled, very fierce, leaping, seething [?], white-topped, joyful, sorrowful [sea].
He carried off the victory of wisdom in the circuit of Ireland, so that he was exalted; wonderful his name; Letha [?] is nurtured, Scotland is filled.
A wonderful lord [?], three leaps [?], with broad bonds [?]; Columba ... labour [?] upon them.
On the clamorous sea, the generosity of the king who ruled thousands, ruler of plains above smooth fortresses, kings, lands.
The Trinity in his possession ... gentle ... [?]; noble with God, to whom evening and morning were plain to see [?].
Shepherd of monks, judge of clerics, more precious than treasures [?] ... royal ... staves [?], plagues [?] by thirties, by hundreds.
Columba, a candle that kindled [?] three laws [?] ... [?] at midnight [?] of the plain of Erc [?].
... [?] he summons [?] the clouds of heaven; protection of my soul, fortress of my grave [?], the descendant of Conall.
The descendant of Conall, famed with victories; fair was his life; he was a ship of wealth; he was a sea of wisdom; the descendant of Conall ... [?] people.
He was a leafy oak, he was protection of the soul, he was a cliff of the glen, he was a sun of monks; great lord [?] was Columba.
Dear was he whose dwelling was a rock beside the great sea [?]; it was a hard place on which lay Columba's bed.
He crucified his body; he ... [?] his fair sides upon the cliff; he chose bold ... [?] the flagstones [?]; he left branches [?].
He left quilts, he left sleep ... [?]; he broke ... [?]; he was for joy [?], with scanty feasts.
He took up books; he gave up in full the possessions of his father; for love of learning he gave up battles [?], he gave up fortresses.
He gave up chariots; he loved ships [?]; an enemy of falsehood [?], a sunlit [?] seafarer; he set off under sail [?] ... [?].
Columba, Columba who was, Columba who will be, Columba ever-living; that is not a protection that is dim [?].
Columba, may we sing [of him] until the meeting of death, after and before ... [?]; round him everyone calls [?], whom we serve.
A great prayer, the prayer of Eithne's son, which is better than treasures: my soul to his right hand, towards the kingdom, before the people of the world.
God ... [?] royal ... [?] in full benefits, with the will of angels, the descendant of Conall's tribe ... [?].
The victorious one [?] said to worship God by nights, by days, with outstretched [?] hands, with fair generosity, with good deeds.
Good was he in the body, Columba, heavenly cleric ... [?] righteous, eloquent [?], of victorious tongue. D. f. a. [= 'He leads from the south', the poem's opening words].
